doc: The South Carolina counties a collision can be recorded in.
The sexes a person on the report can be recorded as.
The plain yes/no answer the form codes as 1 and 2, used by hit and run and by whether a person contributed to the collision.
The yes/no/unknown answer the form codes as 1, 2 and 9.
Work Zone Related prints this legend; the secondary crash, private property and total damage boxes
print none but are coded the same way by the source system, so they share this list rather than each
carrying an untyped code of its own.
Whether the trafficway the collision occurred on carries one way or two.
How the trafficway the collision occurred on is divided.
The type of barrier present at the collision location.
The type of intersection the collision occurred at, or that it occurred at none.
The light condition at the time of the collision.
The weather at the time of the collision; the form records up to two.
The condition of the road surface at the time of the collision.
How the units came together, or that the collision did not involve a motor vehicle in transport.
The first event in the collision that caused injury or damage.
This is not the same list as the unit page's sequence of events, which adds the non-harmful 01-10 codes
this one does not carry, so the two are kept apart rather than merged and filtered.
Where on or off the trafficway the first harmful event occurred.
The collision's relation to a junction, or that it occurred at none.
The roadway or environmental conditions contributing to the collision; the form records up to two.
Whether a school bus was directly or indirectly involved in the collision.
Which part of the work zone the collision occurred in.
The type of work zone the collision occurred in.
Whether someone was present in the work zone; the worker present and law enforcement boxes print the same legend and share this list.
Whether the person the page records is a motor vehicle driver or a non-motorist.
The kind of jurisdiction that issued the driver's license.
What the driver was distracted by at the time of the collision.
The driver's actions at the time of the collision; the form records up to four, in order.
Whether and how far the person was ejected from the vehicle.
How the person was transported to a medical facility, or that they were not.
Which air bags deployed for the person's seating position.
The restraint the person was using at the time of the collision.
What the non-motorist was travelling as, from a pedestrian to a vehicle on rails.
What the non-motorist was distracted by at the time of the collision.
The severity of the person's injury, from none apparent to fatal.
The person's actions or circumstances contributing to the collision; the form records up to two.
What the person was doing immediately before the impact.
The yes/no/unknown/not-applicable answer every safety equipment box on the person page takes.
What the officer suspects the person had been using.
Whether a test was given, refused or is pending; the alcohol and drug test status boxes print the same legend and share this list.
The kind of alcohol test administered.
The kind of drug test administered.
The substance the drug test found, or that it found none.
What the unit was doing at the time of the collision - in transport, parked, or working.
How badly the unit was damaged.
Whether the unit required a commercial driver's license to operate.
Whether the unit was towed, and whether it was disabled.
The compass direction the unit was travelling in, or that it was not on the roadway.
How speed was involved in the collision, if it was.
Where the unit was damaged.
Codes 01 through 12 are the clock positions on the vehicle diagram printed beside the boxes; the rest
are the named areas the legend lists. The initial point of contact and each of the twelve other areas
of damage draw on this same list.
The type of unit, covering both the motor vehicles and the other vehicles the legend lists.
How the unit was being used as an emergency vehicle, if it was.
The special function the motor vehicle was serving, or that it served none.
The events in the collision, in the order they occurred; the form records up to four plus the most
harmful one.
This carries the non-harmful 01-10 codes the collision page's first harmful event list does not, which
is why the two are separate lists over overlapping data.
The grade of the roadway where the unit was travelling.
The alignment of the roadway where the unit was travelling.
What the vehicle was doing immediately before the impact.
The traffic control devices in place where the collision occurred; the form records up to four.
The condition of the vehicle contributing to the collision, or that none did.
